title: Remove the method-presence guards in public/ (prompt-section.js, common.js, dispatch.js, task-page.js); no behaviour change
description:
## Problem: the `querySelector` guards in `public/prompt-section.js`

Seven guards of the form `X.querySelector ? X.querySelector(...) : null` let a stub container without `querySelector` pass through the client. A real DOM always has `querySelector`, so in production the guard is always true. Its only effect is that a test stub which returns `null` takes the null branch, and the real-DOM branch never runs under test.

The seven lines at `origin/main` `1b83bbff` (the HEAD when this ticket was filed):

* `public/prompt-section.js:964`: `const oldQuestion = container.querySelector ? container.querySelector('[data-question-slot]') : null;`
* `public/prompt-section.js:995`: `const fresh = container.querySelector ? container.querySelector('[data-question-slot]') : null;`
* `public/prompt-section.js:998`: `const oldCard = oldQuestion && oldQuestion.querySelector ? oldQuestion.querySelector('[data-testid="session-question-card"]') : null;`
* `public/prompt-section.js:999`: `const freshCard = fresh.querySelector ? fresh.querySelector('[data-testid="session-question-card"]') : null;`
* `public/prompt-section.js:1008`: `const card = oldQuestion && oldQuestion.querySelector ? oldQuestion.querySelector('[data-testid="session-question-card"]') : null;`
* `public/prompt-section.js:1120`: `const oldQuestion = container.querySelector ? container.querySelector('[data-question-slot]') : null;`
* `public/prompt-section.js:1137`: `const el = scope && scope.querySelector ? scope.querySelector('[data-fold-count="sessions"]') : null;`

**Same concept, different spelling, not counted above.** Ten `container.querySelector && container.querySelector(...)` guards at lines 1122, 1147, 1170, 1444, 1559, 1818, 1834, 2024, 2036 and 2811 do the same job. Removal should cover them too, or each remaining one should say why it stays.

**The class is the idiom, not these lines (widened in the LIN-4255 close-out, at** `origin/main 591bb959`**).** A grep for `querySelector[[:space:]]*(\?|&&)` over `public/`, `lib/` and `routes/` finds 20 guards. The 17 above are in `public/prompt-section.js`. Two more are in `public/common.js:1761` and `public/dispatch.js:342`, and one is in `public/task-page.js:717`:

* `public/common.js:1761`: `: scopeEl.querySelector && scopeEl.querySelector('.dispatch-exec-controls'));` (in `readDispatchExecControls`, the path `prompt-section-task-mode` is stopped on, `public/common.js:1758-1763`).
* `public/dispatch.js:342`: `: scopeEl.querySelector && scopeEl.querySelector('.dispatch-preset-select')`.
* `public/task-page.js:717`: `var painted = answer && answer.querySelector ? answer.querySelector('[data-testid="task-page-status"]') : null;`.

All three outside `prompt-section.js` are in scope: remove them, or record on each why it stays. Removal in `common.js` and `dispatch.js` can unblock tests that stub `querySelector` to reach those functions (check `task-page-client` and the other census entries that cover `task-page.js`).

## Why it matters

* LIN-4272 (census close-out) found that `tests/unit/run-limit-gating.test.js:121` and `tests/unit/runner-link-surfaces.test.js:169` stub `querySelector` to return `null` for every selector. Those suites only ever run the null branch of these guards.
* The reader stubs in run-quota and runner-link (`<select>.value`) stay stubs because the fake does not model `<select>.value`. Removing the guards is part of what lets real-DOM reads replace those stubs.
* Parent: LIN-4255 names removing these guards as out of scope. This ticket is that follow-up.

## Acceptance (guards)

* No `querySelector ?` or `querySelector &&` guard remains in `public/prompt-section.js`, `public/common.js`, `public/dispatch.js` or `public/task-page.js`, or each one that remains has a recorded reason.
* Production behaviour is unchanged. Each touched suite keeps its test names and counts, and the full unit suite and E2E pass.
* `run-limit-gating`, `runner-link-surfaces` and `run-quota` no longer stub `querySelector` to `null` where the real DOM can answer.

## Problem: a new `lin-NNNN` witness still reaches for a local stub

The census (LIN-4265) fails any new hand-written fake DOM. It cannot stop a single-element stub that is already on its list, and the list only shrinks. The default for a new witness is still a local stub. LIN-4247 added a hand-written copy four minutes after LIN-4252 merged (LIN-4255 description).

Evidence from LIN-4272's classification at `1b83bbff`:

* 25 census entries remain. 16 are single-element stubs marked "not attempted" that a move could cover with the shared fake as it stands. 9 are stopped on an API the fake does not model.
* `loadWorld` runs its scripts at construction, so a suite cannot set markup first. The live-console suites work around this with `scripts: ['common.js']`. LIN-4289 is that gap.

## Acceptance (witness default)

* A new `lin-NNNN` witness, written by copying the nearest existing one, uses `loadWorld` or `createFakeDom` by default.
* A new `lin-NNNN` test file that defines a `querySelector`-bearing object and does not use `loadWorld` or `createFakeDom` fails a check, with a message that says what to use.
* Any pointer added to `CLAUDE.md` stays within budget. The file is at 110 lines, the cap, and 11,802 of 12,000 bytes (`tests/unit/claude-md-line-budget.test.js:28-29`). A pointer must replace a line, or move content to `docs/architecture/`.

## Options for the witness default (with a recommendation)

1. **Documentation only.** A pointer in `CLAUDE.md`. Cheap, but nothing enforces it.
2. **Guard only.** Extend the census to fail a new `lin-NNNN` file with a stub. It is enforced, but the author still writes the stub first.
3. **Make** `loadWorld` **the cheap path, and add the guard from option 2.** This covers the markup option (LIN-4289) and a one-element helper. **Recommended.** The census treats the symptom. The cause is that `loadWorld` costs more to write than a stub, so the default only changes when the cheap path is cheaper.

## Related

* LIN-4272: the close-out this came from.
* LIN-4255: parent. The guards are its named out-of-scope item.
* LIN-4254: the open move ticket for the remaining fakes. It overlaps with the witness-default problem.
* LIN-4289: the `loadWorld` markup option. It is one piece of the witness-default problem.

## From the area's blind reads (5 Nov, at `591bb9596`): context for the witness-default half

Four blind, code-only reads of the fake-DOM move (LIN-4252 + LIN-4255) scored it better, better. Each named the same residues, and they bear on "make `loadWorld` the cheap path". These are claims for the Survey to check, not facts:

* `clickOn` **exists but is bypassed.** `client-world.js` has "the one element-level click", yet `brief-recap-autogenerate` (`pressDrawn`), `scan-retire-ui` (`press`), `chat-append-options` (`press`) and `prompt-section-look-alike` (`pressNode`) each loop over `btn.listenersOf('click')` themselves.
* **There are three ways to load** `common.js`**'s harness models:** `disclosureWindowStubs` in `real-dispatch-disclosure.js`, an inline `__HARNESS_MODELS__` (`live-console-world.js`, `lin-2933`), and `withHarnessModels` run by hand after `loadWorld({ scripts: [] })` (`observation-ruling-delivery`, `brief-recap-*`). `loadWorld`'s JSDoc describes the choice rather than making it, and it repeats the live-console recipe that `live-console-world.js` owns. The eight observation suites repeat one stub set.
* **A dead workaround:** `real-dispatch-disclosure.js`'s `browserMarkup` decodes `—`/`…` "because the fake does not", but the fake's `NAMED` already has both (`aeb9d877`).
* **A second registry with no guard:** the `fake-dom.js` header's hand-kept, ticket-tagged consumer list, which 13 of 15 commits edited. The census can already derive it. The `<select>.value` stop is written in the header (one file) and in the census comments (three files).
* **Docs that didn't learn:** `CLAUDE.md:58` and the header's first line still say the fake is for `prompt-section.js`/`question-cards.js`.

Runs after LIN-4293, which touches the same question-slot functions as the guards.

## How to go about it (from a Survey before work began)

Both Surveys (on this ticket, 19:09–19:10, at `af55cb737`) and LIN-4272's builder corrected it. **This ticket is now the guards only.** The person's scope call:

1. **Moved out.** The witness-default half and the blind reads' residues above move to **LIN-4297**. Acceptance 3 (stubs replaced by real reads) moves to **LIN-4296**, the shared fake modelling `<select>.value`. Both Surveys found that the stubs are stopped by `<select>.value`, not by these guards. Removing the guards here unblocks nothing, and the PR should say so.
2. **Remove all 20 method-presence guards.**
   * In `public/prompt-section.js`, at the current line numbers (995, 1028, 1031, 1032, 1044, 1156, 1158, 1174, 1184, 1207, 1481, 1596, 1855, 1871, 2061, 2073, 2837, which LIN-4293 moved).
   * Elsewhere: `common.js:1761`, `dispatch.js:342` and `task-page.js:717`.
   * **The paired guards in the same expressions go too** (`.matches &&` at `common.js:1759` and `dispatch.js:340`; `getAttribute ?` at `task-page.js:718`), so that no statement keeps two spellings.
   * Note the `.closest ?` guards (`task-page.js:236/570/652`, `prompt-section.js:2817`): remove them where the same reasoning holds.
3. **Where a guard stays, its reason is written beside it.** For example, an `e.target` that can be a Text node, which has no `closest`.
4. **The other method-presence guards across** `public/` (about 23, in 12 files) are not this ticket. Count them in the PR, for the notebook.
5. **Witness: none new.** Both Surveys show the change is behaviour- and test-neutral: every stub that reaches these lines defines `querySelector` and returns null. So the witness is the unchanged suite (names and counts) plus a green E2E run. The PR shows that `grep -nE "\.(querySelector|matches|closest|getAttribute) (\?|&&)"` is empty, or lists the guards that stay, with reasons.

## At merge

* The grep is empty, or each remaining guard has its reason beside it.
* The full unit suite and E2E pass, with names and counts unchanged.
* The PR says plainly that this unblocks no suite.

## Implementation Plan

*Pruned at close-out (5 Nov 2026). Implemented as approved: all 30 method-presence guards (*`querySelector`*,* `matches`*,* `closest`*,* `getAttribute`*) removed from* `public/prompt-section.js`*,* `common.js`*,* `dispatch.js` *and* `task-page.js`*, keeping every object null check, with no deviations from the plan. PR [https://github.com/JKershaw/LinearViewer/pull/2315](<https://github.com/JKershaw/LinearViewer/pull/2315>) (squash-merged as* `b389f9b0`*; deployed and verified live). The unblocks-no-suite caveat stands (the real stop is* `<select>.value`*, LIN-4296). The full pre-prune description is preserved in the task snapshots, and the plan, trial evidence and review are in the comment trail. Remaining method-presence guards elsewhere in* `public/` *are LIN-4303.*

**Session fit.** fits one session.

parent.title: The shared fake DOM becomes the one in fact: move the hand-written client test fakes onto it, with a census (LIN-4252 tidy-after)

comments.body: Close-out note: priority set to Low (1) because the guards are test-only dead-branch hygiene with no production effect, and the risk is only that new witnesses keep copying the stub pattern. No type label was set: the proxy PATCH has no label field, and the catalog closest fit is `Improvement`. Please apply it by hand.

Close-out note (LIN-4255): description widened to the whole querySelector guard idiom (20 guards: 17 in prompt-section.js, plus common.js:1761, dispatch.js:342, task-page.js:717), per the LIN-4255 review ledger item 4. Acceptance now covers all four files.

## Survey global: LIN-4292 @ af55cb737

**Where it lands.** Two places. (1) `public/prompt-section.js` (~2,900 lines), in the question-slot, fold and run-slot repaint functions that LIN-4293 (af55cb73) just reworked, so every line number in the ticket is now wrong. The grep still finds 20 guards: 17 in `prompt-section.js` (now 995–2837), plus `common.js:1761`, `dispatch.js:342` and `task-page.js:717`. (2) The test harness: `helpers/fake-dom.js`, `helpers/client-world.js` and `fake-dom-census.test.js`. It is improving quickly: nine move PRs this week took the census from 56 to 25 files. 15061f40 already fixed `CLAUDE.md:58` and the header's first line, so that residue from the blind reads is gone. The dead `—`/`…` decode in `real-dispatch-disclosure.js:24` is still there.

**Done the obvious way.**
- Removing the guards is safe for production, but it leaves the idiom half-removed. The guards in `common.js:1759-1761` and `dispatch.js:340-342` are paired with `scopeEl.matches &&` in the same expression, and `task-page.js:718` repeats the idiom as `painted.getAttribute ?`. About 23 method-presence guards of the same kind sit in 12 `public/` files.
- Removing the guards changes no test coverage. `run-limit-gating:121` and `runner-link-surfaces:169` both *define* `querySelector() { return null }`, so the guard is already true and the null comes from the stub. `runner-link-surfaces:169` serves `swipe.js`'s `document` lookups and never reaches these guards. `prompt-section-run-quota` already uses `loadWorld`. Its remaining stub is `readDispatchExecControls` (:70), which is stopped by `<select>.value` (`fake-dom.js:80-85`), not by a guard. The third acceptance bullet really asks for a select model and a move (LIN-4254). This ticket targets a symptom there.
- The witness check: of the 28 `lin-*` files that define a `querySelector`-bearing object, 17 use neither `loadWorld` nor `createFakeDom`. Copying the nearest file still gives a stub most of the time. Thirteen of the 17 are census-listed. Four fall below the census threshold (`lin-3833-client-harness`, `lin-3833-home-mount-needs-you`, `lin-3975-summary-and-time`, `lin-4243-placement`). A rule for "any querySelector-bearing object" contradicts the pinned NEGATIVE fixture "a lone querySelector" (`fake-dom-census.test.js:544`). It also catches arguments to pure functions (`initLocalTimes({ querySelectorAll })`) and needs its own grandfather list. That would be a third hand-kept registry, after `HAND_WRITTEN_FAKE_DOM_FILES` and the fake-dom header's list of about 35 consumers, which `staleFileMessage` already tells every move to edit.
- `CLAUDE.md` is 110 lines and 11,790 bytes, and `:58` already says to use `loadWorld`. No new pointer is needed.

**What this task can carry.**
- Remove all 20 guards, plus the paired `matches`/`getAttribute` guards in the same statements, so no statement keeps two spellings.
- Put the witness rule in the census as a new signal pinned by fixtures, scoped to files that vm-run a `public/` script rather than to `lin-` names.
- Make `loadWorld` the cheap path: a `markup` option (LIN-4289) and one named switch for the `common.js` harness-models route in place of the three recipes the JSDoc describes.
- Derive the consumer list in the fake-dom header from the census and delete the hand-kept copy. Delete the dead decode.

**Better still, but not this task's.** Model `<select>.value`. That unblocks four census entries and the run-quota stub. Move the 16 "not attempted" stubs (LIN-4254). Remove the other method-presence guards across `public/`.

## Survey open-0: LIN-4292 @ af55cb737

LIN-4293 has landed and moved the line numbers. There are still 20 guards. In `prompt-section.js` they're at 995, 1028, 1031, 1032, 1044, 1156, 1158, 1174, 1184, 1207, 1481, 1596, 1855, 1871, 2061, 2073 and 2837. The others are at common.js:1761, dispatch.js:342 and task-page.js:717.

**Why it's hard: removing the guards unblocks none of the suites in "Why it matters".**

- Every stub I found that reaches these lines *defines* `querySelector` and has it return null: run-limit-gating:121, runner-link-surfaces:169, task-mode:32 and task-page-client:406. These suites take the null branch because the stub returns null. The guard plays no part. Removing it is behaviour- and test-neutral, which is good for the "counts unchanged" acceptance. Acceptance 3, though, means moving run-limit-gating and runner-link-surfaces onto `loadWorld`, and that is LIN-4254 work. runner-link-surfaces' `makeEl` stub serves swipe.js's `document.querySelector`, not a prompt-section container.
- The run-quota reader stub and three census stops (task-mode, run-control, settings-take) are stopped on `<select>.value`, not on `querySelector`. `readDispatchExecControls` reads `select.value` (common.js:1765). The fake returns undefined for it and throws on a write (fake-dom.js:80-85). **The deeper fix is to model `<select>.value`.** That frees all four.
- The idiom reaches past the grep. The same expressions are also guarded with `.matches &&` (common.js:1759, dispatch.js:340) and `painted.getAttribute ?` (task-page.js:718). There's also `.closest ?` at task-page.js:236/570/652 and prompt-section.js:2817. If only the `querySelector` half goes, those expressions stay half-guarded. The `e.target` guards have a real reason to stay, since a target can be a Text node. Write that reason down.

**Witness default**

- The check "querySelector-bearing object, no loadWorld/createFakeDom" is stricter than the census, which needs 3 or more tree members. A naive matcher already catches 18 existing `lin-*` files:
  - `lin-4035` is a false positive: it uses `loadWorld` through `live-console-world.js`, so the check has to follow helpers.
  - Four aren't on `HAND_WRITTEN_FAKE_DOM_FILES`: `lin-3833-client-harness`, `lin-3833-home-mount-needs-you`, `lin-3975-summary-and-time` and `lin-4243-placement`.

  Telling "new" files apart means either a second list that only shrinks (the hand-kept registry the blind reads criticise) or a git-diff rule.
- Without LIN-4289, an enforced default pushes authors to `scripts: []` and running the loaders by hand. That is the third `common.js` loading path, the one the ticket wants gone. Option 3 depends on LIN-4289 landing first.

**Stale at BASE**

- 15061f40 already fixed CLAUDE.md:58 and the header's first line.
- CLAUDE.md:58 already points to `loadWorld` and the census. Option 1 is in place, so a pointer would edit that line. The file is at 110 lines and 11,790 bytes.
- Still true: the `—`/`…` decode in `browserMarkup` is dead. Six test files loop `listenersOf('click')` and five use `clickOn`.

**First**

1. Run the proposed matcher against the current tree before building the check. The 18/4/1 split decides how the baseline works and whether a threshold is needed.
2. Ship the guard removal as a small PR of its own, with reasons recorded on the `e.target` guards. Don't count it as unblocking anything.
3. File `<select>.value` as the real unblocker for run-quota and runner-link.

PR: https://github.com/JKershaw/LinearViewer/pull/2315 (branch feat/lin-4292-remove-method-presence-guards, commit 48d58f70)

Removed all 30 method-presence guards (querySelector / matches / closest / getAttribute) in public/prompt-section.js, common.js, dispatch.js and task-page.js. Object null checks are kept, so each replacement returns the same value as before on a real DOM. Grep for the idiom in the four files: 30 hits before, 0 after.

Unblocks no suite: the stubs that reach these lines already define querySelector and return null. The real stop is <select>.value in the fake (LIN-4296).

Verification:
- Unit suite: 23,749 pass / 0 fail, test-name list identical to af55cb73 baseline.
- E2E: 2,004 pass / 1 skipped (existing runtime skip), second run. The first run had one failure (lin-4010 Escape drawer, a null boundingBox at a repaint) that did not recur; it passes 5/5 in isolation on both branch and baseline.
- Secret scan passes.
- CI on PR 2315: all checks green (Unit tests, E2E shards 1-4, Secret scan).

Left in place, outside the named methods: slot.contains && (prompt-section.js:1210) and two typeof ...querySelectorAll checks (prompt-section.js:881, common.js:2356). 12 named-idiom hits remain in 8 other public/ files, out of scope.

## Review — LIN-4292

PR https://github.com/JKershaw/LinearViewer/pull/2315, head `48d58f70` on base `af55cb73` (still origin/main; no other commit has touched the four files since the ticket was filed).

CI: green on `48d58f70`. Unit tests, E2E shards 1–4, Secret scan and CI success all pass, and the PR is MERGEABLE.

**Scope against the plan.** The diff touches only the four planned files, 30 lines in and 30 out, and matches the plan's 30-hit list line for line. The plan's grep `\.(querySelector|matches|closest|getAttribute)[[:space:]]*(\?|&&)` gives 18/4/2/6 hits at base and **0 on the head**. I re-ran it myself. Every object null check from the old expressions is still there (`oldQuestion ?`, `scope ?`, `answer ?`, `painted ?`, `root ?`, `e.target ?/&&`, `t &&`, `scopeEl &&`). On a real Element each rewrite returns the same value as before. I traced the callers of `readDispatchExecControls` and `readDispatchPresetPicker` (dispatch.js:168-169, feedback-widget.js:431, prompt-section.js:2496/2741, app.js:1615). Each one passes an Element or null, never `document` or a fragment, so the unguarded `scopeEl.matches` cannot throw. The PR says plainly that it unblocks no suite and names LIN-4296 (`<select>.value`) as the real stop, as the plan required. No witness-default or census rule was added, which is right per the scope call.

**Regression check.** `git log -15` over the four files shows LIN-4293, 4246, 4247, 4048, 4243 and others. None of them added or relied on these guards, and nothing was reverted. The keepTypedQuestion and readerFocusIn call sites from LIN-4246 and LIN-4293 keep their order and their null checks.

**Isolated, or one of a class?** It is one of a class: DOM method-presence guards. The plan bounded this ticket to four named methods in four files and set `slot.contains &&` (prompt-section.js:1210) aside on purpose. The siblings below fall outside that bound:
- In the four files, under a different spelling (`!X.querySelectorAll`): `prompt-section.js:1872` (`!drawer.querySelectorAll`, the line right after one this PR edited), `task-page.js:415` and `task-page.js:429`. The PR's "left in place" list leaves these three out. It names only 1210, 881 and common.js:2356. **Outside** (different method, and the plan drew the line at four methods).
- 12 hits of the named idiom in 8 other `public/` files. The PR counts them. **Outside** (the plan excluded them).

Close-out should file one follow-up for "method-presence guards beyond the four methods/files", covering the 12 hits plus the 3 `querySelectorAll` and 1 `contains` above. Check first that LIN-4297 does not already cover it. Close-out should also fix the PR body's "left in place" line so it lists all six (1210, 881, 1872, common.js:2356, task-page.js:415, 429).

**Test quality and mutation check.** The ticket adds no new test. The witness is the unchanged suite. I ran the 227 unit files that load any of the four scripts on the head: 5,361 pass, 0 fail. Then I removed each null-object check the PR claims to keep, one at a time, and reverted each after the run:
- `oldCard = oldQuestion ? … : null` → unguarded: 9 fail
- `card = oldQuestion ? …` (focus path): 309 fail
- fold `scope ? …`: 46 fail
- task-page `answer ? …`: 3 fail
- task-page `painted ? …`: 3 fail
- `runOptsOf` `root ? …`: 17 fail
- task-page:570 `e.target ? …`: **0 fail**
- common.js:1759 `scopeEl &&`: **0 fail**

So the suite does witness the kept null checks, except two. Those two are older null checks this PR did not change (no null `e.target` click, and no `readDispatchExecControls(null)` test). That is an existing gap, not a defect in this PR. I note it but do not ask for it here.

**E2E.** The implementer's first run failed once in `lin-4010-home-opened-task` "Escape closes it". That spec drives `keepFocusInDrawer`, which this PR touched (prompt-section.js:1871). I re-ran the whole spec on the head with `--repeat-each=4`: **44/44 passed**. CI's E2E shards are green too.

**Checklist.** Tests cover the change (unchanged-suite witness, mutation-checked above). No new state, security, error-handling or performance surface. Style matches the file.

### What CI Did Not Prove
- **Inside** (a claim this change depends on, the plan's `.closest`/`.matches` event-target removal). Real-browser event targets for the six unguarded event-target calls (`common.js:1868/1871` on document `change`, `prompt-section.js:2817` `change`, `task-page.js:570/652` `click`) must always be Elements. Before, a non-Element target took the null branch. Now it throws `… is not a function` in the listener. The unit fakes cannot show what a real browser does. E2E drives some of these listeners, not all six. Code read: the listeners sit on form controls and buttons, `change` and `click` targets are Elements in current browsers, and the only synthetic dispatches in `public/` (`decision-panel.js:74/75/92`) target Elements. Only third-party script dispatching on `document` could hit it. **Route: named rollback.** Revert `48d58f70`. It is a pure client-side change with nothing persisted and no consumer. The failure is loud (a console TypeError at that listener), and nothing else is lost.
- **Inside**, discharged. The implementer's lin-4010 "Escape closes it" failure on a touched function: re-run 44/44 on head `48d58f70` (above), and CI E2E green.

### Verdict
Approve — conditional on close-out discharging the ledger.

The guard removal is complete against the plan's 30 places, value-preserving on a real DOM, and the kept null checks are mutation-witnessed. For close-out:
1. Amend the PR body's "left in place" list as named above.
2. File the out-of-scope follow-up for the remaining method-presence guards, after checking LIN-4297.
3. Record the named rollback (revert `48d58f70`) for the event-target item.

## Close-out — LIN-4292

**Merged:** PR https://github.com/JKershaw/LinearViewer/pull/2315, squash-merged as `b389f9b0` (pinned with `--match-head-commit 48d58f70`). Main had moved by three docs-only commits since the review's base `af55cb73`, with no code files touched, so CI on `48d58f70` still stood. Deployed: Harbour production deployment for `b389f9b0` succeeded, and the live footer shows `b389f9b0`.

**CI on the merged head `48d58f70`:** green. Unit tests, E2E shards 1-4, Secret scan (source) and CI success all passed. A CI workflow exists (`.github/workflows/test.yml`), so no substitute run was needed.

**Verified on what landed:** the guard grep (`\.(querySelector|matches|closest|getAttribute)[[:space:]]*(\?|&&)`) is empty on `b389f9b0` in all four source files. The four `public/` scripts served live by Harbour (`/prompt-section.js`, `/common.js`, `/dispatch.js`, `/task-page.js`) returned HTTP 200 with 0 hits each. There were no other post-deploy steps.

**Changes I made after the approval** (nobody reviews these after me; none touch code, so the head commit is unchanged):
- Amended the PR body's "Left in place" line to list all six places (`prompt-section.js:1210`, `:881`, `:1872`; `common.js:2356`; `task-page.js:415`, `:429`), which answers review close-out item 1. No commit; the PR description was edited.

**Ledger:**

No related tickets were settled by this work (LIN-4296, LIN-4297, LIN-4254 and LIN-4289 remain open for their own scope). The ticket had no type label, so I applied `Improvement`.

## Survey 1a (round 3)

**1. Why was it difficult?** It wasn't, in the code. The plan named every line, and each edit was one line: drop the method test, keep the object test. The only care needed was matching values exactly, so `x && x.m ? x.m(s) : null` became `x ? x.m(s) : null`. The time went on proof. E2E takes 8 minutes, and the `lin-4010` Escape drawer test failed once with a null `boundingBox` at a repaint. Clearing it took a second full run plus 5/5 in isolation on both the branch and base.

**2. What I'd do first.** Run base E2E alongside the base unit run, so a failure could be diffed by name straight away. I'd also grep my four files for the behaviour, not the ticket's regex, which would have caught the spellings in 5.

**3. What I'd tidy.** The same idiom was still in my files under other spellings. `!drawer.querySelectorAll` sat in `keepFocusInDrawer`, a function I had just edited, and `slot.contains &&` sat two lines below another of my edits. So a function could still mix two spellings. "No half-removed expression" held only per statement. LIN-4304 has since cleaned these up.

**4. What the ticket would have been.** One ticket: "an Element is trusted to have its methods; a check over `public/` enforces it." The removals would follow from that rule. LIN-4304 turned out to be that ticket, an AST scan with an allow-list where each entry gives its reason.

**5. What the ticket and plan got wrong.**
- The original acceptance said removing the guards would unblock suites. It didn't, and the Survey caught that before I started.
- The count moved from 7 to 17 to 20, then 30 at HEAD.
- The main error: the grep was the definition of done, and it only matched `.m ?` and `.m &&`. It missed `!x.m` and `typeof x.m === 'function'`. LIN-4304 later removed six of those in my four files (`prompt-section.js:881`, `:1210`, `:1872`, `common.js:2356`, `task-page.js:415`, `:429`).

**6. What the change left behind.**
- **Nothing new and nothing duplicated.** A stub missing a method now throws loudly instead of quietly taking a null branch.
- **Nothing enforced the rule.** The census covers fakes, not production guards, so the remainder lived only in my PR text until LIN-4304 added the check.
- **One real case was allow-listed.** `close-out-client.test.js` hand-builds documents, so three guards in `close-out.js` were kept for a reason. That reason was outside my files.

**7. Where the line should have been.** The four files were the right call: verifiable and test-neutral, with a trial behind them. The four method names were the wrong axis. The line should have been the behaviour in any spelling, within those files. That was about six more one-line edits and the same suites, so widening within the files carried no new risk. The narrow line cost a second PR (#2320) that evening, editing lines two away from mine. It also let my grep report the files as clean when they weren't. Drawing it by spelling made "done" mean "the regex is empty", a weaker claim than the ticket's goal.
